subject: Startups
title: Peter Thiel's $500K Facebook Bet
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Peter Thiel's $500K Facebook Bet.

hook.text: In 2004, Peter Thiel wrote a $500,000 check to a college kid with a website for Harvard students.

buildup.text: Facebook had just a few thousand users at Ivy League schools. Revenue was zero. Most investors stayed away.

discovery.text: Thiel saw something others missed: insane engagement. Students checked Facebook multiple times per day.

twist.text: That $500K bought 10.2% of Facebook. When it went public, Thiel's stake was worth over $1 billion.

climax.text: One check, one insight about user engagement, and patience turned half a million into a billion-dollar return.

punchline.text: A $500K bet returned $1 billion. Engagement was the signal.

quiz.question: What signal convinced Peter Thiel to invest in Facebook?
